recipes.name: Mango-licious Tilapia
ingredients_raw: crushed red pepper flakes to taste
3 roma tomatoes - peeled, seeded and chopped
1 jalapeno pepper, seeded and finely chopped

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Combine orange juice, olive oil, orange zest, salt, black pepper, and pepper flakes in a shallow baking dish. Rinse and pat dry tilapia fillets; place into the baking dish and turn to coat with orange juice mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until tilapia easily flakes with a fork, 10 to 12 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine tomatoes, mango, onion, avocado, cilantro, jalapeño, lime zest and juice, ginger, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt in a glass bowl; set aside at room temperature while tilapia cooks. Place fillets on a platter; spoon salsa over top to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Mango-licious Tilapia
raw_recipe.description: This mango-licious tilapia recipe features mango salsa over tilapia. Serve tilapia over brown rice. The salsa is great as a dip or on cottage cheese, too.

review.reviewBody: this was exceptional! I added pineapple to the mango salsa mix and used powdered ginger that I had laying around. I also just used half a can of diced tomatoes rather than cutting up roma tomatoes. The presentation was virtually identical to the picture but I laid down a bed of fluffy instant rice, then a layer of mango salsa, then th e tilapia, then a topping of mango salsa with avocados and steamed broccoli rounding up the corners. A mango margarita makes a perfect accompaniment. It was fantastic!

Loved this recipe! The flavors were very eclectic, but really made the tilapia taste great. I grilled the tilapia on an infrared grill, placing the tilapia on a boat made of foil after pouring the orange sauce over it. Instead of the cilantro, onion, jalepeño and tomato I opened a can of store brand tomatoes with chilies (similar to Rotel). Made short work of the chopping. It made a great, light meal with snow pea pods.

YUM! I have made this recipe several times now, and it has become a family staple. The main change I do is puree some of the ingredients to make a marinade, and put it in a ziploc with the fish for an hour or so while I prep the rest of the meal. It is versatile to various citrus you have on hand. I have used a combination of orange, lime, and lemon, adding honey to sweeten if it comes out too sour. No red pepper. Pureed the onion, ginger (1 tsp dried ginger since I didn't have fresh on hand), cilantro, and 3 cloves fresh garlic with the juices and olive oil, added salt, and marinated all that together with fish for 30-60 min in a ziploc bag. Put diced mango, cilantro, tomato, and red bell pepper on top of fish and broiled in oven until done. SOOO good!

This was delicious ! We marinaded the fish in orange juice and fresh basil for one hour. Substituted parsley for the cilantro. we added fresh basil at the end. Next time I will cut back on the lime and let it sit together for a awhile longer to let the flavors really blend. We grilled the fish using a grill mat and used a bit of smoke. was really a great dish!

This was very good! I left out the salt, added a diced red bell pepper and about a clove of minced garlic and used a bit less of the mango and red onion. I prepared the salsa early in the day so the flavors had a chance to blend, adding the diced avocado about 30 minutes before serving. Marinated the Tilapia for a couple of hours in the OJ and Zest. Served with Refried Beans, Sweet Corn Cake and some rice I had leftover from the night before. Family truly enjoyed, and thanks!

I will be making this again and again... :) I really enjoyed how the flavors came together. I added pineapple to make it sweeter. I did not have avocado so I'm looking forward to trying the original recipe next time. I served the fish over white rice. I added 1/4 c orange juice, orange zest and a pinch of kosher salt to the rice in order to give it some flavor and tie the dish together. Also, I will let the fish marinate for at least 30 minutes next time.

This was very delicious. Followed the previous recommendation to add pineapple. I used salmon instead of tilapia. The prep took forever though, took me at least an hr just to get everything chopped. Ready in 22 minutes? Yeah right, maybe if you’re splitting all the peeling, chopping, zesting, etc between 2-3 people. So you might as well marinate the fish in the mixture while you chop up everything for the salsa. Very delicious, but very labor intensive in my onion.

I followed this loosely, and used what I had. I mixed the orange juice with thai chili sauce (the sweetish kind that you dip spring rolls in.) I salt and peppered the fish and marinated it in the juice mixture for an hour, flipping intermittently. For the salsa, I just used finely (confetti) diced mango, pickled jalapeno, cilantro, half a clove of garlic, and some lime juice, and salt. I baked the fish right in the marinade, for a bit longer than you said. About 20 min. We like it well done, and it thickened the sauce. It was awesome. I wish I'd had some avocado to dice into the salsa.

I made this tonight with my daughter, She loved helping and I love introducing her to new ingredients, it makes her more open to try new things if she helps prepare the dish. This was one of the best salsas I have ever made/tasted! So many wonderful flavors. I doubled the recipe so it took almost an hour of prep but well worth it, Oh and the tilapia was just as awesome! We all loved it!!!
Wife just made this and it is fantastic. Like one reviewer said we added pineapple and eliminated the red pepper flakes. So refreshing and light. This will be a regular meal for us. Thank you.

I saved this recipe in 2011 and I really wish I had made it before now. This is delicious and so easy! I did the fish on the grill in a disposable aluminum pan. The fish sort of poached in the orange juice mixture. Served over coconut rice with edamame (from Cooking Light) with the salsa on top. I am making again this week!
Used frozen mahi mahi and served with coconut rice made in the Insta pot. Husband loved it! The rice went really well with the fish and salsa too!
Great. We usually use a little extra mango and a little less onion and cilantro. This dish is eash to shape to your personal taste preferences.

Absolutely Delicious! Very fresh and lite meal. Fresh cilantro would have been better but I did not have any as it is winter. I followed the recipe exactly as written. Definitely going to make this again.

Delicious!! The only changes I made was I added some diced strawberries to the salsa. Maybe a 1/2 cup. I only used 1/2 a red onion because that's what I had on hand. Thank you for sharing this delicious recipe!!!

Absolutely delicious! My family loves it. I'm not an experienced cook so it took me about an hour to prep, not 10 minutes. I don't normally have fresh ginger or cilantro at home. It was well worth it though! I will double the recipe next time to have extra salsa for tortilla chips.
I did not have an avocado or fresh tomatoes, so I made the mango salsa without them. It was great! The fish poaches and does not have a strong flavor, but with the salsa it is great.
Turned to be the best tilapia I ever had. Really happy meal
